testCase.description: DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: example "trim(" abc ") = "abc"". Normative example of the new trim function (DMN17-96).
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: example "trim("x ") = "x"". Normative example: trailing white space removed.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: example "trim("") = """. Normative example: empty string stays empty.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: example "trim(null) = null". Normative example: null argument gives null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: trim(string): "return a string with white spaces (see rule 61 of the grammar) removed from the beginning and the end". Derived: a string without leading or trailing white space is returned unchanged.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: trim(string): "return a string with white spaces (see rule 61 of the grammar) removed from the beginning and the end". Derived: only the beginning and the end are trimmed; inner white space is preserved.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: trim(string): "return a string with white spaces (see rule 61 of the grammar) removed from the beginning and the end". Derived: a string made only of white space trims to the empty string.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.1.2 grammar rule 61: "white space = vertical space | \u0009 | \u0020 | \u0085 | \u00A0 | \u1680 | \u180E | [\u2000-\u200B] | \u2028 | \u2029 | \u202F | \u205F | \u3000 | \uFEFF", rule 62: "vertical space = [\u000A-\u000D]". Derived: tab (\u0009) and vertical space (\u000A, \u000D) count as white space for trim; written with FEEL string escapes (rule 64).

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.1.2 grammar rule 61: "white space = vertical space | \u0009 | \u0020 | \u0085 | \u00A0 | \u1680 | \u180E | [\u2000-\u200B] | \u2028 | \u2029 | \u202F | \u205F | \u3000 | \uFEFF", rule 62: "vertical space = [\u000A-\u000D]". Derived: non-ASCII white space from rule 61 (no-break space, en quad, zero width space, ideographic space, BOM) is trimmed, not only \u0020.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.1.2 grammar rule 61: "white space = vertical space | \u0009 | \u0020 | \u0085 | \u00A0 | \u1680 | \u180E | [\u2000-\u200B] | \u2028 | \u2029 | \u202F | \u205F | \u3000 | \uFEFF", rule 62: "vertical space = [\u000A-\u000D]". Derived: \u200C (zero width non-joiner) is outside [\u2000-\u200B] and is not white space, so it is kept and the length stays 4.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: parameter is named "string" in "trim(string)". Derived: named-parameter invocation (Table 64).

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: the parameter domain of trim is "string". Derived: a number argument gives null.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.3 Table 75: trim(string) has one required parameter. Derived: invoking it with no arguments gives null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.1.2 grammar rule 61: "white space = vertical space | \u0009 | \u0020 | \u0085 | \u00A0 | \u1680 | \u180E | [\u2000-\u200B] | \u2028 | \u2029 | \u202F | \u205F | \u3000 | \uFEFF", rule 62: "vertical space = [\u000A-\u000D]". Derived: the remaining code points listed in rule 61 (\u0085, \u1680, \u180E, \u2028, \u2029, \u202F, \u205F, \u000B, \u000C, \u2001, \u200A) are all trimmed; \u180E is listed by rule 61 even though current Unicode no longer classes it as white space.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.1.2 grammar rule 61: "white space = vertical space | \u0009 | \u0020 | \u0085 | \u00A0 | \u1680 | \u180E | [\u2000-\u200B] | \u2028 | \u2029 | \u202F | \u205F | \u3000 | \uFEFF", rule 62: "vertical space = [\u000A-\u000D]". Derived: control characters outside rule 61 (\u0001, \u001F) are not white space and are kept (unlike e.g. Java String.trim, which strips every character up to \u0020), so the length stays 5.
